samples.summary: ~300-line untrusted-clipboard sanitization layer is unrequested scope for issue #783
samples.evidence: The task spec (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md) scopes the change to: document `Block.headingLevel` retention, add `unlistedBlockType`, preserve the level in `MemDocStore.setBlockType` / `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType`, route the three `toggleList`s and the two keyboard exits through the helper, plus unit tests. Nothing in Problem/Approach/Steps asks for clipboard payload validation. This diff adds a complete hand-rolled schema validator (`sanitizeBlock`, `sanitizeInlineStyle`, `sanitizeTableData`, `sanitizeCellStyle`, `asStoredColor`, `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, id regeneration, ~300 src lines + ~90 test lines + a design-doc section) which changes paste behaviour for every block/inline/table field, not just `headingLevel`. That is a separate hardening concern (its own issue + design entry) riding along with a two-field model change, and it broadens the blast radius of a regression fix well past the acceptance criteria.

samples.summary: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (offset-0 split moves the remembered level) contradicts the plan's stated Non-goal on splitting
samples.evidence: The spec's Non-goals say: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today. ... `applySplitBlock` keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half. Only the block that was actually bulleted remembers." The diff introduces an exception (offset 0 moves the memory), and to honour it adds a shared predicate plus new CRDT writes in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock` (`removeStyleByPath(['headingLevel'])` and stamping the attr onto the new node) — new collaborative-edit surface not covered by the plan. Either the plan's Non-goal should be amended explicitly, or this exception belongs in a follow-up; as written the diff both asserts the Non-goal (docs.md) and carves an exception into it.

samples.summary: DOCX `<w:pStyle>` heading-level coercion is unrelated hardening, in an area the plan lists as a non-goal
samples.evidence: The plan's Non-goals include "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`", and the diff nonetheless edits `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` to `Number()`/`trunc`/clamp the level plus three new tests, motivated by clipboard-injection hardening rather than by the un-list regression. It also duplicates a clamp that already exists for the same value in `packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:108` (`Math.min(6, Math.max(1, block.headingLevel ?? 1))`) — a shared `clampHeadingLevel` (one already exists in `serialize/markdown.ts`) would be the reuse-friendly home.

samples.summary: Paste-fold provenance rules (`foldedHeadingLevel`) and the empty-list-item split workaround bundle extra behaviour/bug-fixes beyond the issue
samples.evidence: `foldedHeadingLevel` plus the `splitExitsList` branch in `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts ~3609) change paste semantics and fix a pre-existing, issue-independent ordering bug (`Doc.splitBlock` short-circuiting on an empty list item interleaving pasted blocks). Neither is in the plan's Steps. The empty-list-item paste bug in particular is a distinct defect that deserves its own change/issue rather than being folded in, and the workaround duplicates knowledge of `Doc.splitBlock`'s list-exit special case in the view layer instead of giving the model a split API that doesn't short-circuit.

samples.summary: Sanitizer re-declares model unions and re-implements `normalizeBlockStyle` instead of reusing model helpers
samples.evidence: `BLOCK_TYPES`, `ALIGNMENTS`, `LIST_KINDS`, `UNDERLINE_STYLES`, `STRIKE_STYLES`, `VERTICAL_ALIGNS`, `BORDER_KINDS` restate unions declared in `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts` with no compile-time tie (no `satisfies readonly BlockType[]`), so adding a `BlockType` silently makes it unpasteable; `sanitizeBlockStyle`/`sanitizeCellStyle` re-implement the `{...DEFAULT_*, ...partial}` merge that `normalizeBlockStyle` (types.ts:280) already provides. Also `MAX_LIST_LEVEL = 8` is a third copy of the ceiling already hardcoded in `view/editor.ts:2883` and `view/text-editor.ts` indent paths.

samples.summary: Validation added only at the clipboard edge while the CRDT/tree deserializer still trusts the same attribute
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs.md now claims `headingLevel` "round-trips through the Yorkie tree node attributes and the backend `docs-tree` serializer like any other block attribute" and that clipboard input is narrowed to 1–6, but `docs-tree.ts:408` still does an unchecked `Number(attrs.headingLevel) as DocsBlock['headingLevel']`, and `YorkieDocStore`'s block cache builder likewise coerces without range checking. If the intent of this change is to make an out-of-range/non-numeric level unrepresentable, the layer chosen (one view-level deserializer) leaves the model's other ingress points asserting a guarantee they do not enforce.

samples.summary: Entry-parity guard regex-parses source text where a namespace import comparison would do
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports()` reads `src/index.ts` / `src/node.ts` with `readFileSync` and a regex over `export { ... } from '...'`. Importing both entries (`import * as browser from '../../src/index.js'`) and diffing key sets would express the same invariant without a brittle source-text parser that silently returns an empty set (and passes) if the export style changes to `export * from`.

finding.summary: ~300-line untrusted-clipboard sanitization layer is unrequested scope for issue #783
finding.evidence: The task spec (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md) scopes the change to: document `Block.headingLevel` retention, add `unlistedBlockType`, preserve the level in `MemDocStore.setBlockType` / `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType`, route the three `toggleList`s and the two keyboard exits through the helper, plus unit tests. Nothing in Problem/Approach/Steps asks for clipboard payload validation. This diff adds a complete hand-rolled schema validator (`sanitizeBlock`, `sanitizeInlineStyle`, `sanitizeTableData`, `sanitizeCellStyle`, `asStoredColor`, `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, id regeneration, ~300 src lines + ~90 test lines + a design-doc section) which changes paste behaviour for every block/inline/table field, not just `headingLevel`. That is a separate hardening concern (its own issue + design entry) riding along with a two-field model change, and it broadens the blast radius of a regression fix well past the acceptance criteria.

verdict.reason: The sanitization code exists exactly as quoted (clipboard.ts:32-332: sanitizeBlock, sanitizeInlineStyle, sanitizeTableData, sanitizeCellStyle, asStoredColor, MAX_LIST_LEVEL, MAX_TABLE_DEPTH, id regeneration), so the presence claim is factually accurate — but it is not a blocking design-fit violation under this lens's rubric. (1) It is causally tied to this change rather than unrelated hardening: the change's own paste path now adopts a clipboard block's headingLevel into the destination via foldedHeadingLevel (text-editor.ts:47, 3634, 3665) applied to blocks returned by deserializeClipboard(json) from the attacker-writable WAFFLEDOCS_MIME flavour (text-editor.ts:1240-1242). Before this change no clipboard block-level attr crossed into the destination block. (2) The canonical subsystem design doc documents it as part of that mechanism, folded into the existing heading-memory section rather than a parallel file (docs/design/docs/docs.md:225-235, following :190-224), so design-doc discipline is met. (3) None of the rubric's four major triggers applies: no acceptance criterion fails, no duplicate/parallel doc, no reinvented module (no other block-payload validator exists in packages/docs/src or core), and the task's stated Non-goals (todo:49-58 — list-item styling, split propagation, DOCX pStyle) do not cover clipboard validation. (4) The finding's sole basis — absence from Problem/Approach/Steps — is undercut because the Steps list (todo:36-47) is demonstrably non-exhaustive of the change: it also omits mergeDropsHeadingMemory and the insertBlocks provenance work that the lessons file (:22-28) and design doc (:190-224) show are in-scope parts of the same fix. What remains is a taste objection that the validator is broader than strictly needed for headingLevel, which is a minor approach preference and never blocks.

finding.summary: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (offset-0 split moves the remembered level) contradicts the plan's stated Non-goal on splitting
finding.evidence: The spec's Non-goals say: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today. ... `applySplitBlock` keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half. Only the block that was actually bulleted remembers." The diff introduces an exception (offset 0 moves the memory), and to honour it adds a shared predicate plus new CRDT writes in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock` (`removeStyleByPath(['headingLevel'])` and stamping the attr onto the new node) — new collaborative-edit surface not covered by the plan. Either the plan's Non-goal should be amended explicitly, or this exception belongs in a follow-up; as written the diff both asserts the Non-goal (docs.md) and carves an exception into it.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out verbatim. `splitMovesHeadingMemory` exists at packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:290-302 and is applied in `applySplitBlock` (lines 260-266) to move `headingLevel` from the `before` half to the `after` half on an offset-0 split — so the plan's assertion that `applySplitBlock` "keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half" is no longer true. The exception also adds new collaborative CRDT writes in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock`: `removeStyleByPath(..., ['headingLevel'])` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2030 and stamping `afterAttrs.headingLevel` at 2062-2067. The originating plan's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:53-57) still state the opposite and were not amended; its Steps (36-47) list no split work and the lessons file (22-28) records only "a split must not copy it onto the new bullet" plus the merge rule. docs/design/docs/docs.md both restates the Non-goal (172-177) and carves the exception (179-188). This is an exceeded/contradicted stated Non-goal with unrequested scope into the CRDT split path — `major` by this lens's rubric. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable via `Doc.splitBlock` on both stores, and the concern (scope creep vs. the issue's Non-goals, spec/doc conformance) is in this lens's lane rather than a line-level correctness matter.

finding.summary: DOCX `<w:pStyle>` heading-level coercion is unrelated hardening, in an area the plan lists as a non-goal
finding.evidence: The plan's Non-goals include "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`", and the diff nonetheless edits `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` to `Number()`/`trunc`/clamp the level plus three new tests, motivated by clipboard-injection hardening rather than by the un-list regression. It also duplicates a clamp that already exists for the same value in `packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:108` (`Math.min(6, Math.max(1, block.headingLevel ?? 1))`) — a shared `clampHeadingLevel` (one already exists in `serialize/markdown.ts`) would be the reuse-friendly home.

verdict.reason: All claimed facts check out in the tree. docx-style-map.ts:95-103 contains exactly the Number()/trunc/clamp coercion, with an in-code comment motivating it by untrusted clipboard/import payloads and XML attribute injection — not by the un-list regression. docx-style-map.test.ts:101-115 adds the three corresponding tests with the same injection rationale. The plan at docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:58 lists "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`" as a Non-goal, and its Approach/Steps (lines 18-47) contain no export-layer work — line 24-26 argues export readers are already guarded and need no change. The duplication claim also holds: the same 1-6 clamp of the same value sits at model/named-styles.ts:108 and a named helper clampHeadingLevel already exists at serialize/markdown.ts:128-132 (used at line 104), so this is a third inline copy. Scope creep into a stated Non-goal plus duplication of an existing helper are both major-kind under the design-fit rubric; nothing supports not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
